fact: La Nation reports that Djibouti Telecom, Ethio telecom and Sudatel signed a tripartite agreement in Djibouti on 4 February 2026 for the construction and maintenance of the Horizon cross-border terrestrial fibre link joining Djibouti, Ethiopia and Sudan.

On Monday 7 September 2026 the three operators presented Horizon in Addis Ababa to hyperscalers, carriers and vendors in a pre-commercialisation phase, seeking partner interest and feedback before deployment and commercial launch; the document describes the infrastructure as future.

Tech Africa News reports that Ethio telecom has moved from planning into active deployment of the Horizon Fiber corridor linking Djibouti, Ethiopia, Sudan and Jeddah, with end-to-end architecture finalised and site-material procurement and delivery complete so physical deployment can proceed.
The document states a memorandum of understanding for Horizon Fiber was signed in Addis Ababa on 3 December 2024 and a binding agreement followed on 4 February 2026.

Connecting Africa reports that Ethio Telecom, Djibouti Telecom and Sudatel turned their December 2024 Horizon Fiber memorandum into a binding agreement for a terrestrial corridor from Djibouti's landing stations through Ethiopia to Sudan's; the document gives no signing day, so its published date is used.

BTW Media analysis states the sources it reviewed announce no capacity purchase, paying customer or service start date for Horizon, which partners had only presented to potential users in Addis Ababa.
The document refers to the official announcement of 4 February 2026 of an agreement for a terrestrial fibre corridor joining Djibouti's cable landing stations to Sudan's via Ethiopia.

Telecom Review Africa reports that Ethio telecom, Djibouti Telecom and Sudatel converted their December 2024 memorandum into a binding agreement on the Horizon Fiber terrestrial corridor from Djibouti's landing stations through Ethiopia to Sudan; the document gives no signing day, so its published date is used.

ITWeb reports Ethio telecom, Djibouti Telecom and Sudatel Group signed a binding tripartite agreement to operationalise the Horizon Fiber Initiative, a terrestrial fibre corridor linking Djibouti's submarine cable gateways through Ethiopia to Sudan; signing date is taken from the article's date, 2026-02-06.

La Nation reports the three operators signed on 4 February 2026 in Djibouti the agreement launching Horizon, a terrestrial fibre corridor of nearly 2,800 km with 144 fibre pairs linking Djibouti, Addis Ababa and Port Sudan, to be built.
La Nation states the contract follows a memorandum of understanding signed in Addis Ababa on 4 December 2024 by the three operators.

SUNA reports Sudatel signed on 4 February 2026 a strategic agreement with Djibouti Telecom and Ethio telecom launching Horizon Fiber, a terrestrial fibre corridor linking Djibouti's submarine cable stations through Ethiopia to Sudan.

fact: Ethio telecom's release states it signed on 4 February 2026 with Djibouti Telecom and Sudatel Group a tripartite agreement under the Horizon Fiber Initiative for a terrestrial fibre corridor connecting Djibouti's landing stations, traversing Ethiopia, to Sudan's landing stations.
Ethio telecom's release states the agreement builds on a memorandum of understanding signed in Addis Ababa on 3 December 2024.

TechAfrica News reports Ethio telecom, Djibouti Telecom and Sudatel signed a tripartite contractual agreement on 4 February 2026 in Djibouti to implement Horizon Fiber, a cross-border fibre corridor from Djibouti's landing stations through Ethiopia into Sudan.

Ethio Telecom, Djibouti Telecom and Sudatel Group signed a strategic agreement under the Horizon Fiber Initiative, 'last week' relative to the 2026-02-11 article, to build a cross-border terrestrial fibre corridor linking Djibouti's submarine cable landing stations via Ethiopia to Sudan's landing stations.
The February 2026 agreement builds on a memorandum of understanding the three telcos signed in Ethiopia in December 2024 on establishing a secure alternative international route.

Birr Metrics reports that Ethiopia's Horizon Fiber Initiative is a trilateral agreement with Djibouti Telecom and Sudan's Sudatel to establish a multi-terabit terrestrial fibre link by April 2025; the story gives no signing date, so it is dated by its publication.
